title: Queen's Gambit Declined (2...e6)
intro: Black holds d5 with 2...e6. Pressure d5 with Nc3 and Bg5, avoid the Elephant Trap, and target the isolated pawn against the Tarrasch.

lessons.title: The Classical QGD
lessons.summary: Develop Nc3, Bg5, e3 and Rc1 against 2...e6.

steps.text: With 2...e6, Black keeps a pawn on d5. White develops pieces that add pressure to d5.
Develop your queen's knight and attack d5.
steps.hint: Bring the b1 knight to c3.
steps.ifRight: Now two white pieces attack d5.

steps.text: Pin the knight that guards d5.
steps.hint: Put your dark-squared bishop on g5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Bg5 to pin the f6 knight to the queen.
steps.ifRight: Black must unpin or reinforce d5.

steps.text: Support d4 and open the diagonal for your light-squared bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.e3 so your f1 bishop can develop to d3 or e2.
steps.ifRight: White is ready for Nf3, Rc1 and Bd3.

steps.text: After 5...O-O 6.Nf3 Nbd7, put your queenside rook on the key open file.
steps.hint: Move the a1 rook onto the c-file.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Rc1 (or 7.Qc2) to build pressure down the c-file.
steps.ifRight: Wait until Black moves the f8 bishop before playing Bxc4, saving a tempo.

lessons.title: The Elephant Trap & Semi-Slav
lessons.summary: Meet 4...Nbd7 with 5.e3 and handle the Semi-Slav calmly.

steps.text: If Black plays 4...Nbd7 instead of 4...Be7, they set a famous trap if White tries to win the d5 pawn after cxd5 exd5.
Reinforce d4 calmly instead of rushing.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.e3 to protect d4 and stay completely safe.
steps.ifRight: White develops Nf3 and Bd3 next with zero danger.

steps.text: Here White traded 5.cxd5 exd5. Do not fall for the Elephant Trap. Play a sound move.
steps.hint: Support d4 with e3 or develop Nf3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.e3: taking on d5 loses a piece to 6...Nxd5 7.Bxd8 Bb4+.
steps.ifRight: Safe and solid, keeping White's edge.

feedback.c3d5: 6.Nxd5 loses a piece after 6...Nxd5 7.Bxd8 Bb4+ 8.Qd2 Bxd2+ 9.Kxd2 Kxd8.

steps.text: If Black sets up the Semi-Slav triangle early with 3...c6, White stops ...e5 and prepares e3.

steps.ifRight: Now White can meet 4...Nf6 calmly with 5.e3.

steps.text: After 4...Nf6, support d4 calmly and avoid messy gambit lines.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.e3: after 5...Nbd7, 6.Bd3 or 6.Qc2 gives a sound, pleasant game.
steps.ifRight: White develops Bd3 and castles cleanly.

lessons.title: Meeting the Tarrasch (3...c5)
lessons.summary: Isolate the d5 pawn with cxd5 and target it with g3 and Bg2.

steps.text: In the Tarrasch Defence, Black hits your centre right away with 3...c5.
Create a target on d5 by trading pawns.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.cxd5 so Black is forced to take on d5 with an isolated pawn.

steps.text: Develop your king's knight and control e5 and d4.
steps.ifRight: Next White targets d5 from the long diagonal.

steps.text: Prepare to fianchetto your light-squared bishop onto the h1-a8 diagonal to attack d5.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.g3: Bg2 and O-O put lasting pressure on Black's isolated d5 pawn.
steps.ifRight: With Bg2 and O-O coming, d5 will be under fire for the whole game.
